name: TxEcosystemTesting
title: Terminology Ecosystem Tests: a TestPlan and Gherkin for the HL7 terminology server test set
description: A test guide for FHIR terminology servers. It declares, as one TestPlan and 38 Gherkin feature files, the test cases of the HL7 terminology-ecosystem test set, and states what is under test as a requirements CapabilityStatement. The test cases are generated from the upstream tests/test-cases.json and fetch the upstream expected responses at run time, so they cannot drift from the source.
disclaimer: This is not an approved HL7 test specification.
blurb: The test cases are HL7's, taken from the Terminology Ecosystem IG. What this guide adds is their
expression as a TestPlan and as Gherkin for the Interoperability Test Bed, so that they can be run
from a test bed rather than only from the FHIR validator's built-in runner.
testingPageSummary: What is under test, how the upstream test set maps onto the plan, how a test decides, and how the scripts are packaged.
artifactsSummary: The test plan, the requirements CapabilityStatement that says what is under test, and the Gherkin scripts.

testingTitle: One plan, one system under test
testingIntro: This guide declares its tests with the [TestPlan](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-testing-ig/en/StructureDefinition-TestPlan.html) resource from the [FHIR Testing IG](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-testing-ig/en/) (`hl7.fhir.uv.testing`). There is **one** plan, because there is one thing under test: a FHIR terminology server. Its `scope` points at the [requirements CapabilityStatement](CapabilityStatement-tx-server-requirements.html), which is what a system has to offer for the plan to apply to it.
The upstream test set is already grouped into suites, and those groupings become `TestPlan.suite`.

testingSections.title: From the upstream test set to this plan
body: | Upstream | Here |
| A suite of `test-cases.json` | `TestPlan.suite`, with `suite.input.file` naming its feature file |
| A test | `suite.test`, matched to a `Scenario:` by name |
| The scenario's `Then` steps | `suite.test.assertion.human` |
| The suite's `setup` resources | a table in the feature's `Background:`, sent with every request as `tx-resource` parameters |
| `http-code` | an assertion that the status matches that class, rather than 200 |
| `Accept-Language`, a custom `header` | a `set header` step before the operation |
| `profile`, `lenient-display` | merged into the request `Parameters`, so the reader sees what the server receives |
| `version` (4.0, 5.0, !4.0) | a generator filter; the tests left out are named in each feature's header |
The four upstream tests bound to a FHIR 5.0 server are left out: these features are generated for
a FHIR 4.0 server. Regenerating with `--fhir-version 5.0` swaps them back in.

testingSections.title: How a test decides
body: The upstream expected-response files are **matchetypes**: they use `$id$`, `$uuid$`, `$instant$`,
`$choice:...$` and `$optional-properties$` for what may legitimately differ between servers and runs.
A test does not carry a copy of the expected response. It fetches the upstream file at run time from
[the Terminology Ecosystem IG](https://github.com/HL7/fhir-tx-ecosystem-ig) and asks the FHIR
validator's matchetype service to compare the server's answer with it. So the expectations cannot
drift from the source, and taking up a newer test set means re-running the generator rather than
editing this guide.
Where upstream accepts more than one answer - a flat expansion, a second error shape, or
tx.fhir.org's own - the test lists each acceptable file and one match is enough.
A suite with an upstream **mode** other than `general` is expected only of a server that supports
it: the `tx.fhir.org` suites are that server's internal quality assurance, and `snomed`, `omop`,
`icd-11` and `mimetypes` apply where the server carries that content.

testingSections.title: Running the tests
body: The scripts are written in the OTB Gherkin language (generation 2) for the
[Interoperability Test Bed](https://www.itb.ec.europa.eu/docs/guides/latest/). A run needs three
things to reach each other: the terminology server under test, a FHIR validator that serves the
matchetype comparison, and the upstream test material over HTTP.
The same test cases run without a test bed, straight from the FHIR validator, which carries its own
runner:
java -jar validator_cli.jar txTests -tx {server url} -output {folder}
The two runners judge a response differently today. The validator's own runner normalises the
server's answer before comparing (it sorts parameters by name, expansion codes by code, and issues
by severity, and strips `issue.diagnostics`); the matchetype service the Gherkin calls does not, and
does not honour `$optional-properties$` either. A server that is right but answers in another order
therefore fails here and passes there. That gap belongs to the matchetype service, not to these
test cases.

plans.title: Terminology Server
plans.scopeDescription: A FHIR terminology server: the operations of the terminology module, as the requirements CapabilityStatement of this guide states them.
plans.summary: a FHIR terminology server, tested with the HL7 terminology-ecosystem test set
plans.planDescription: The HL7 terminology-ecosystem test cases for a FHIR terminology server, as Gherkin.
plans.resourceDescription: The HL7 terminology-ecosystem test cases for a FHIR terminology server, grouped into the suites the test set defines.
plans.intro: Test plan for a **FHIR terminology server**, as described by the [requirements CapabilityStatement](CapabilityStatement-tx-server-requirements.html) this guide publishes.
plans.description: The test cases are the HL7 terminology-ecosystem test set ([Terminology Ecosystem IG](https://github.com/HL7/fhir-tx-ecosystem-ig), `tests/test-cases.json`), expressed as Gherkin for the [Interoperability Test Bed](https://www.itb.ec.europa.eu/docs/guides/latest/).
plans.note: The expected responses are not copied into this guide: a test fetches the upstream file at run time and compares the server's answer with it as a matchetype, so the expectations cannot drift from the source.
plans.purpose: To declare, in a machine-readable and runnable form, the behaviour a FHIR terminology server must demonstrate to be considered conformant with the HL7 terminology-ecosystem test set.
